articles.title: Stanford Engineers Teach Spacecraft to "Dream" Their Way to the Space Station
articles.description: Docking with the ISS may seem simple. However, actually doing so is a showcase in how difficult orbital mechanics can be. It’s equivalent to traveling down a highway at 28,000 km/hr and parallel parking into an open garage on a multi-billion dollar laboratory traveling at the same speed. If you try to accelerate forward you actually drift up, and there’s no air friction to naturally slow you down. Oh, and if you hit the lab, everyone onboard both your craft and the station dies, and the resultant debris field could both wipe out dozens of satellites and even people on the ground. No pressure, obviously. For decades, aerospace engineers have been docking successfully using hard coded physics equations and human pilots to correct them. But now, a new paper, available in pre-print on arXiv from researchers at Stanford, is taking a shot at building an AI to perform a series of “mental simulations” that could fundamentally change how future spacecraft interact with each other.

articles.title: Engineering the Substation Exit for Reliability, Capacity, and Expansion
articles.description: This white paper gives distribution engineers and utility teams a practical overview of the substation exit, the short and high-consequence section where station capacity divides into individual feeders. It explains how covered, spacer-supported overhead construction can reduce common contact-driven faults while leaving room for future circuits. What you will learn about: Why a fault near the substation exposes more customers than one farther along the feeder, and why the first spans out of the station carry so much reliability weight. How covered conductors and spacer-cable systems differ from bare overhead conductors, and why covered conductor is not treated as touch-safe insulation. Which engineering factors shape a sound exit design, including conductor rating, protection coordination, grounding, and structural loading. How overhead spacer cable compares with conventional bare overhead and underground shielded cable across footprint, reliability, and lifecycle cost. How to move a project from concept to commissioning using staged design gates and a clear performance specification. Download this free whitepaper now!

articles.title: Carly Rae Jepsen works round-the-clock in Day and Night
articles.description: Music history is full of excellent releases made in the wake of new motherhood - from Lauryn Hill's Miseducation to Eartheater's Heavenly Body this year. Carly Rae Jepsen has a habit of releasing albums in two, typically releasing a B-side album for each cycle. These storied traditions came together on Sept. 18 for Day and Night , the pop star's eighth studio release and first double album arriving right after the birth of her first child. While not quite her Ray of Light , this outing features a tremendous expansion of Jepsen's sonic palette and some more feathers in the cap of contemporary pop's most consistent should've-been-a-hit-maker. With 24 songs for 24 hours, the album is split into 'day' and 'night' sides. The Day side songs share an autumnal wistfulness with a focus on live instrumentals Jepsen hasn't spotlighted so strongly since her debut . The Night side gives her classic synthpop a clubbier spin. There's no doubt Jepsen had little difficulty filling up 84 minutes - fans will recall her claims of writing 200 songs for Dedicated . The diverse production choices help the time go by quickly, but I question the inclusion of some of these tracks (' That's Just Me " goes in one ear and out the other). The album's singles are well selected for the most part. " On Wires " and " After All " mark the public's introduction to the album's day side, and both remain among the strongest tracks on the record. The emphatic guitar-driven chorus of "On Wires" (with the classic Jepsen brass in the back of the mix) marks a radical departure from her typical sound. Meanwhile, "After All," a soulful and hazy fall-time picture of family life, opens the album as a natural evolution of the disco sounds from her previous The Loveliest Time . The Night side was represented in the singles department by " Don't Leave Me on the Dancefloor ," which evokes ABBA in its bright piano keys and Robyn's patent ' sad banger ' style. " Motivation " marks well-explored territory as a catchy, almost embarrassingly sincere dance-pop ode to found family. The single " Versailles ," released alongside the album, is perhaps most telling for Jepsen's intentions with her latest project. Stuttering piano appears and disappears as she switches in and out of a slower, ballad-esque tempo and a dance track to dissolve in. These adventurous production choices crop up in several other tracks, from the mild psychedelic distortions in " Something Tragic " to the closer of the Day side, " Just a Little Walk on the Moon ." Her vocals in the bossa nova influenced song sound like they're emerging from an evening radio, as the album prepares for the night side of life. " Gimme your time, gimme your nights, gimme your days " she demands on " Habits of Creatures " - and who can deny her? Jepsen's B-sides do tend to have the better songs - I staunchly maintain both Dedicated: Side B and The Loveliest Time are superior to their A-side counterparts - and this double album does not mark an exception. While the stripped back and instrument-based soundscape of the Day side do not always synergise with the pop star's strengths, her forays into new dancefloor territory on the Night side yield more consistently magical results. " Never Let a Good Thing Die " immediately launches listeners from the Day side into the club, pulsating with jittery beats before expertly transitioning into an expansive outro. Right after, " Amalfi Coast " recalls Jessie Ware's nu-disco while blending a vocoder and synth to glorious house effect. Jepsen does not stray far from her usual lyrical grounds across the album, but in " Patience Power Passion " she delights in the irresistible bounce of the chorus , while in " Diver " she pulls out enough metaphors to please a high school English teacher. Her warehouse of dance references expands with the build-up to the garage-style beat of " Near or Far ," merging with her poppy sensibilities where " No Labels, I Love You " conjures up classic house for everyone to get up and dance. Fittingly, she draws the curtains on " Super Sage ," an ethereal and enveloping track filled with love. Day and Night is among Jepsen's more mellow and less immediate records, along the tone of The Loneliest Time . It is also perhaps her most ambitious album so far - released during one of the busiest periods of her life (keep an ear out for her upcoming 10 Things I Hate About You musical ). "My joke is that I'm at some point going to write a memoir, and it'll be called The Year We Did Everything at Once, " she described in an interview with Elle . For an album which reflects this breadth, all of it - the new, the familiar, the great, the less-good - feels at home in the sonic world she has constructed in her musicianship. This stylistic expansion is a new springboard to continue growing her flawless discography (yes, including Tug of War ). As the world of dance-pop evolves, Carly Rae Jepsen strengthens her niche and keeps her loyal listeners excited to run away with her once more.

articles.title: Strange Galaxies in the Early Universe Were Shaped by Weird Stars
articles.description: Galaxies and their stars in the early Universe look a lot weirder than those we see today, and astronomers want to know why. A team of researchers at the University of Utah decided to survey certain stars in nearby galaxies as analogs of those that existed when the Universe was still in its infancy. The survey, called the "Treasury of Extremely Metal-Poor O Stars (TEMPOS), used the ultraviolet (UV) light streaming from those relatively close-by stars as detected by the Hubble Space Telescope's Cosmic Origins Spectrograph.

articles.title: In House primaries, organized groups may matter more than voters
articles.description: In most of the nation's 435 congressional districts, the general election is not much of a contest. With the vast majority of U.S. House seats considered safe for one party or the other, the primary usually determines who goes to Congress—and it is the election Americans know the least about. A new book co-authored by a researcher at the Annenberg Public Policy Center (APPC) of the University of Pennsylvania finds that voters are rarely the most important influence on the outcome.

articles.title: Fluorescence timing identifies eight proteins in one cell with a single staining step
articles.description: An international collaboration led by the University Medical Center Göttingen (UMG), Germany, has developed a labeling method that distinguishes fluorescent labels not by color but by how long it takes a dye to emit fluorescence. This makes it possible to visualize eight different proteins in a cell simultaneously in a single step using standard microscopes. The results have been published in the journal ACS Nano.

articles.title: Political shifts may shape how quickly Germany adopts electric cars and solar power
articles.description: A new study conducted by the Climate Action Research Lab (CARL) at the University of Freiburg finds that electric cars and photovoltaic systems are less widespread on average in municipalities with strong support for Alternative for Germany (AfD). The researchers also examined how changes in political support within the same municipalities over time affect subsequent adoption of these technologies. They found that an increase in the AfD's share of the vote is followed by relatively slower adoption of electric cars and photovoltaic systems. The technologies continue to spread, but at a slower rate. The work is published in the journal Nature Sustainability.

articles.title: How Diffractive Solar Sails Could Stop a Killer Asteroid at 100 km/s
articles.description: Asteroids don’t come with a warning label that they might one day hit Earth. While we don’t know of any currently on course to do so, we are finding thousands of new ones each year, and there’s always a potential that one could. We proved a viable technique for dealing with that eventuality - the DART mission successfully moved a small asteroid using a “kinetic impactor” - basically a big rod designed to push the asteroid off its trajectory. But DART had one big flaw - it was traveling in the same direction as the asteroid, and approached it from behind, eventually hitting it with an impactor launched while in orbit around it. That technique might work if we have enough warning, but would require years of orbital mechanical maneuvering to pull off. An alternative, proposed by researchers at Beihang University, is to use a new type of solar sail to deflect a potentially hazardous asteroid by hitting it head on.

articles.title: Pigeons' proposed inner-ear compass runs into a noise problem
articles.description: A pigeon turning its head might seem an unlikely electricity generator. Yet one proposed explanation for the bird's magnetic sense depends on exactly that: Turning through Earth's magnetic field would produce tiny electrical signals inside its ears. However, a theoretical study suggests that this miniature generator cannot supply directional information fast enough to work as a compass. The problem is electrical noise produced within the proposed sensor itself.
